name: Aspirin + Clopidogrel
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Acute coronary syndrome or ST-elevation myocardial infarction in patients already taking both drugs
usual_adult_dose.dose: One tablet once daily (clopidogrel 75 mg/aspirin 75 or 100 mg); duration per indication (up to 12 months after NSTE-ACS or PCI)

key_interactions.action: Avoid; pantoprazole has a smaller effect.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors, SSRIs, heparin, thrombolytics, GP IIb/IIIa antagonists
Strong CYP2C19 inducers (rifampicin); ritonavir- or cobicistat-boosted regimens

serious: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis (rare)
Acute kidney impairment (rare, mainly with pre-existing dysfunction)

contraindications: NSAID or aspirin hypersensitivity (asthma, rhinitis, nasal polyps)

pk.half_life: Clopidogrel about 6 hours (inactive metabolite 8 hours); aspirin 0.3 to 0.4 hours; salicylic acid about 2 hours
pk.half_life_eskd: At CrCl 5–15, clopidogrel platelet inhibition about 25% lower; bleeding time similar
pk.metabolism: Clopidogrel: prodrug activated partly by CYP2C19; aspirin hydrolyzed to salicylic acid
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Clopidogrel about 50% in urine, 46% in feces (120 hours); salicylate renal excretion depends on urine pH

sources.citation: European Medicines Agency. (n.d.). DuoPlavin (clopidogrel/acetylsalicylic acid): EPAR product information [Summary of product characteristics]. Sanofi Winthrop Industrie. Retrieved November 17, 2026.
